accuracy.evidence: Matches CCSS K.NBT.1 and 1.NBT.2.b: 11-19 as ten ones and some further ones. Lab uses ten-frame + leftover ones; equations 10+n; excludes calling 10 a teen.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets counting only leftovers, digit swap (41), two tens, treating 10 as a teen, reading 11 as 'two ones' with no ten. Challenge feedback names each.

lab_distinct.evidence: Focused on teen composition 11-19 with ten-frame leftovers, not general two-digit chart work (flagbundle) or bonds to 10 (flagnbonds).

lab_teaches.evidence: Fill ten → add ones → read → split → build discovers 10+n before the text labels it.

predictions.evidence: Tempting wrongs: 4 instead of 14, 2 instead of 12, 6 tens for 16 — classic teen slips the tasks disprove.

challenge_feedback.evidence: why() covers ones/swap/two/left/thirty/look/teen with specific corrections tied to 10+n.

readability.evidence: Kid text stays on ten-frame and leftover ones; adult cites K.NBT.1 / 1.NBT.2.b and names mistakes.

no_filler.evidence: No throat-clearing; each paragraph adds compose, decompose or digit meaning.

mobile.evidence: Large taps on frame and answer tiles; button twins; young styling.

accessibility.evidence: Every action has a button; aria-label updates; challenge buttons labelled.
